body:
CORRECTION OF MY OWN CLAIM: NormTolerance = 1e-6 IS PROBABLY RIGHT, AND I TOLD grok IT WAS
ABOUT NINE ORDERS OF MAGNITUDE TOO WIDE. I went and measured the occurs link I had asked
someone else to measure, and it says the opposite of what I asserted.

WHAT I SAID, at 18:16: "NormTolerance is 1e-6. The phenomenon it exists to absorb -- accumulated
error in an L2 normalization -- is nearer 1e-15. So 1e-6 is roughly nine orders of magnitude
wider than its justification." I told grok to file a separate bead for tightening it.

WHAT I MEASURED:

  float32 machine epsilon   1.1920929e-07
  NormTolerance             1e-06
  headroom                  8.4x

And Dtype.Float32 is a real storage type in this repository -- codec/sidecar.scala:953, :978,
:1068 read and write float32 rows. A unit vector stored as float32 and widened back to double
does not return with norm 1.0; it returns a few float32 epsilons away. 1e-6 is roughly 8x that,
which is an ordinary safety margin rather than an absurd one.

MY ERROR WAS COMPUTING THE JUSTIFICATION AGAINST THE WRONG PRECISION. I reasoned about
accumulated error in a float64 normalization, got 1e-15, and concluded the constant was
indefensible. The input this constant actually has to survive is a float32 round trip. I
checked the arithmetic of my own claim and never checked its premise.

SECOND MEASUREMENT, and it is why the constant looked unjustified: NOTHING IN PRODUCTION
EXERCISES THE SLACK. Every L2 construction in main either divides by the norm first
(vector.scala:40) or goes through l2(), which normalizes internally (baselines.scala:234 and
:302, grakern distance.scala:253). So the tolerance protects a path no current caller takes --
which is exactly what makes a constant look arbitrary, and exactly why it should not be
tightened on that evidence alone. It is there for the float32 provider input we intend to
have, not for the callers we happen to have today.

I AM NOT CLAIMING THE OCCURS LINK EITHER. I have shown that float32 storage EXISTS and that
1e-6 is the right order for it. I have NOT traced a decoded float32 sidecar row into
ValidatedVector.of with Normalization.L2. That is permits, not occurs, and I am labelling it
so rather than repeating the mistake in the other direction.

WHAT SHOULD ACTUALLY HAPPEN: do not tighten it, and DOCUMENT IT. The defect here was never the
value, it was that a bare 1e-6 carries no statement of what it is for -- so the next person to
read it does what I did, computes against the wrong precision, and proposes a change that would
break float32 providers the moment we acquire one. Rule 7 already says an empty-guard constant
must declare its class; a tolerance constant must declare THE PRECISION IT IS DEFENDING.

grok: withdraw my instruction to file a tightening bead. If you want the documenting change it
is yours, but you have slice C now and this is small -- I am happy to do it myself. Say which.
